meta.policy: Every source below was fetched and read this session (2026-11-10) with the research retrieval tool. Regulator/statute sources are primary law; the HSBC tariff is primary only for HSBC's own published fees. English translations of PRC rules are reference translations; the Chinese text prevails. A source marked 'fetched' means the document body was retrieved and quoted this session; 'search-surfaced' means the official page was located via search but the body was not re-fetched this session and is not relied on for a numeric claim.

sources.title: SAFE Detailed Rules on Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (Huifa [2007] No. 1, amended republication 2024-04-30)
sources.facts: Art. 2: annual facilitation quota USD 50,000 equivalent per person for settlement and domestic-individual purchases; within quota ID-only at bank. Art. 13(1): foreign individuals purchase FX for lawful current-account RMB income earned in China with ID + transaction-amount materials including tax vouchers. Art. 13(2): reconversion of unused previously exchanged RMB with ID + original exchange memo (valid 24 months); <=USD 500/day (<=USD 1,000 airside before departure) ID-only. Art. 14: domestic individual outward remittance from FX savings account <=USD 50,000/day ID-only, above with authenticity documents. Art. 15: foreign individual outward remittance from FX savings account with ID. Art. 20: emigrant/inheritor property transfer per separate rules. Art. 30: foreign-cash withdrawal >USD 10,000/day requires advance SAFE filing. Art. 39 penalty clause repealed by Huifa [2023] 8.

sources.title: 2026 personal FX FAQ (08): How does a foreign individual purchase and remit labor remuneration earned in China? (2026-07-13)
sources.locator: Full Q&A; cites Current-Account FX Business Guidelines (2020) Huifa [2020] 14 Art. 59
sources.facts: Foreign individuals' lawful current-account RMB income earned in China is purchased into FX at a bank with valid ID and source-of-funds materials showing the transaction amount, including tax vouchers. No annual cap is stated for this documented-income route.

sources.title: 2024 current-account FX policy Q&A case (9): Do foreign individuals enjoy the annual facilitation quota? (2024-06-21)
sources.facts: Foreign individuals purchase FX for lawful current-account RMB income with ID + source materials including tax vouchers; only holders of the PRC Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card enjoy the annual facilitation purchase quota.

sources.title: Administrative Rules on Individual's Foreign Exchange, PBOC Decree [2006] No. 3 (English)
sources.facts: Art. 7: no evasion of limit administration by splitting large amounts into small batches; no fabricated commercial bills/vouchers. Art. 9: annual limit; above it, current-account business with ID + transaction-amount materials. Art. 13: non-domestic individual may convert legitimate current-account RMB income and remit abroad with ID + documents.

sources.title: Regulations of the PRC on Foreign Exchange Administration (State Council Decree No. 532, 2008 revision)
sources.facts: Art. 5: state does not restrict current-account international payments/transfers. Art. 39 (evasion): order to repatriate, fine up to 30%; serious 30-100% + criminal liability. Art. 40 (fraudulent FX purchase): order to re-exchange, fine up to 30%; serious 30-100% + criminal. Art. 42 (unlawful carrying): warning, fine up to 20%. Art. 45 (illegal FX dealing): warning, confiscation, fine up to 30%; serious 30-100% + criminal. Art. 52(2): domestic individual includes a foreign national continuously resident in China for 1 year or more.

sources.title: Circular on Regulating Large-sum Overseas Cash Withdrawals with Bank Cards (Huifa [2017] No. 29)
sources.facts: Overseas cash withdrawals with domestic bank cards: <=RMB 100,000 equivalent per person per civil year across all cards; excess suspends overseas withdrawals current + following year. Per-card daily ceiling RMB 10,000 equivalent. Borrowing/lending cards to evade prohibited.

sources.title: Measures for the Administration of Carrying Foreign Currency Cash In and Out (Hui Fa [2003] No. 102)
sources.facts: Carry out <=USD 5,000 equivalent: no permit. USD 5,000-10,000: bank-issued carrying permit. >USD 10,000: in principle not allowed; SAFE special-case permit only. Same-day repeat travelers: <=USD 500 (2nd+ exit); 15-day repeats: <=USD 1,000 (2nd+ exit).

sources.title: Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC (7th amendment 2018-08-31, official English)
sources.facts: Art. 3: comprehensive income 3-45% progressive; business operation 5-35% progressive; interest/dividends/leasing/transfer/incidental flat 20%. Art. 6(1): resident comprehensive income taxable after RMB 60,000 annual deduction plus special/itemized deductions. Art. 1: resident = domiciled or 183+ days in tax year.

sources.title: Provisional Administrative Rules on Sales and Payment of Foreign Exchange for Personal Asset Outbound Transfer (PBOC, 2004-12-14)
sources.facts: Emigrant asset transfer = assets obtained before immigration permission; inheritor = foreign citizens/HK-Macau residents inheriting China assets. Assets must be legal, owned, undisputed. Apply to SAFE at original registered residence. Emigrant transfers >RMB 200,000 in installments (first <=half; remainder at 1yr and 2yrs) per 2004 text; inheritance lump sum or installments. NOTE: 2014 lump-sum amendment not re-fetched this session (flag F04).

sources.title: Notice on Further Preventing and Disposing of Virtual Currency and Related Risks (Yinfa [2026] No. 42, 2026-02-06)
sources.facts: Virtual currency has no legal status as currency; virtual-currency-related business is illegal financial activity; fiat-crypto exchange strictly prohibited; overseas providers may not illegally serve domestic subjects; financial institutions may not provide accounts/transfers/settlement for it. Repeals Yinfa [2021] No. 237.

sources.title: Report of Foreign Bank and Financial Accounts (FBAR) — IRS page
sources.locator: Who must file; When to file; Penalties
sources.facts: U.S. person with financial interest/signature authority over foreign financial account(s) with aggregate value >$10,000 at any time in calendar year must file FinCEN Form 114 via BSA E-Filing. Due April 15, automatic extension to October 15. Whether account produced income is irrelevant. Civil maximums adjusted annually for inflation per 31 CFR 1010.821; IRS warns its figures may not be current.

sources.title: 31 CFR 1010.821 — Penalty adjustment and table (FinCEN)
sources.facts: For penalties assessed on or after January 17, 2025: 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(B)(i) non-willful max $16,536 (statutory $10,000); 31 U.S.C. 5321(a)(5)(C)(i)(I) willful max $165,353 (statutory $100,000).

sources.title: IRM 5.21.6 — Foreign Financial Account Reporting (2025-02-04)
sources.facts: Willful FBAR violation (on/after 2004-10-23): greater of 50% of account balance or $100,000 (statutory; inflation-adjusted max per S12). Non-willful: up to $10,000 statutory (adjusted per S12); reasonable cause considered. Form 8938 does not replace FBAR; file each form whose threshold is met.

sources.title: IRM 8.11.5 — International Penalties, IRC 6038D (Form 8938) (2025-09-29)
sources.facts: Form 8938 failure: initial $10,000 per form per year; continuation $10,000 per 30-day period after 90 days' notice; max additional $50,000; max total $60,000 per form. No return required = no Form 8938 required even above threshold.

sources.title: Summary of FATCA reporting for U.S. taxpayers (Form 8938 thresholds)
sources.facts: U.S.-resident unmarried: >$50,000 year-end or >$75,000 any time; MFJ: >$100,000/>$150,000. Living abroad unmarried: >$200,000/>$300,000; MFJ abroad: >$400,000/>$600,000. Form 8938 does not relieve FBAR filing.

sources.title: 26 U.S.C. 988 — Treatment of certain foreign currency transactions (2024 edition)
sources.facts: Sec. 988 does not apply to a personal transaction entered into by an individual. If nonfunctional currency is disposed of by an individual in a personal transaction, no gain recognized by reason of exchange-rate changes after acquisition — unless the gain that would otherwise be recognized exceeds $200.

sources.title: Foreign Tax Credit — How to figure the credit (Form 1116)
sources.locator: Figuring the credit; Foreign Tax Credit limit
sources.facts: Credit = foreign tax paid/accrued or, if smaller, the FTC limit. Limit = total U.S. tax x (foreign-source taxable income / total taxable income). Figured on Form 1116. Unused credits carry back 1 year, forward 10 years. Treaty special rules may apply (Pub. 514/901).

sources.title: Know Before You Go: Traveling Abroad — Currency Reporting (CBP)
sources.facts: Travelers entering the U.S. carrying over $10,000 (or foreign equivalent) in currency/monetary instruments must file FinCEN Form 105 with CBP. Threshold applies to individual or traveling group combined. E-file at fincen105.cbp.dhs.gov; must arrive at port of entry within 72 hours or re-file. NOTE: older CBP URL /travel/international-visitors/bringing-money-or-monetary-instruments returns 404 (flag F06).

sources.title: Yearly average currency exchange rates (IRS)
sources.locator: Yearly average table, China Yuan row
sources.facts: China Yuan yearly average: 2025 = 7.129 CNY per USD (2024 = 7.189; 2023 = 7.075). IRS states it has no official exchange rate; accepts any posted rate used consistently. Used here ONLY as a labeled reference conversion for comparing published CNY fees, not as an executable quote.

sources.title: Tariff of Accounts and Services for Wealth and Personal Banking Business (HSBC China, effective 31 Oct 2026)
sources.facts: Outward TT issuance (2.2.4.1): Premier/Advance 0.1% of remittance, min CNY 100, max CNY 500 per transaction, plus cable (2.2.4.2) CNY 120/cable. Private Banking individual: Free. Optional Pay Exact CNY 200. Global Transfer to self (2.2.6.1): Private Banking Free, Premier Free, Advance CNY 145 indicative / actual USD 20 per transaction. International Education Payment (2.2.7): Advance USD 7 — NOT a general remittance price. Premier eligibility requires e.g. TRB >=CNY 500,000 (Note 3). Charges exclude other institutions/government charges (Note 7).

sources.title: China — Tax treaty documents (IRS)
sources.facts: IRS publishes the 1984 U.S.-China Income Tax Treaty PDF and Technical Explanation. Withholding-rate articles were NOT re-fetched this session; any treaty withholding percentage is therefore left blank and flagged (F05), not asserted.
